articles.title: UConn men’s basketball moves up to No. 3 in AP Top 25
articles.summary: The Huskies are up one spot after two wins last week.
articles.body:
UConn men's basketball moved up one spot in this week's poll to No. 3 after convincing wins over Wagner and Ohio State last week. The 4-0 Huskies are behind just No. 1 Florida and No. 2 Michigan State in the polls. Over at KenPom, UConn is ranked No. 8 overall, with the 17th-best offense and seventh-best defense in the country.

Despite losing Duke transfer Nik Khamenia to a foot injury in last Monday's win over Wagner, the Huskies navigated some first-half foul trouble to cruise to a win over an unranked but tough Ohio State team . This week, UConn has only one game on its schedule, but it's a big one, as the Huskies head west to take on No. 12 Arizona on the road in a top-15 matchup.

Arizona stayed at No. 12 for the second-straight week, but is still a top-10 team nationally according to KenPom. Duke, which UConn faces in Las Vegas on Nov. 23, fell three spots to No. 5 after losing to Michigan State in the Champions Classic last week.

Future opponent Virginia rose to No. 4 this week, while Illinois dropped seven spots to No. 10. Kansas jumped four spots to No. 11. While all five of those upcoming matchups figure to be tough without Khamenia, help may soon be on the way as Solo Ball was cleared for full-contact practice with the team as of today.

St. John's remains the only other ranked Big East team in the polls, with the Johnnies ranked at No. 13. Xavier was the only other school in the conference to receive votes.

articles.title: Manchester United have set their sights on move for Premier League defender
articles.summary: Manchester United weigh Calvin Bassey transfer as January plans take shapeManchester United are seriously considering a move for Calvin Bassey as Mauricio Po...
articles.body:
Manchester United weigh Calvin Bassey transfer as January plans take shape

Manchester United are seriously considering a move for Calvin Bassey as Mauricio Pochettino and the club hierarchy shape their defensive plans for January, with TeamTalk reporting that the Fulham defender is seen internally as a strong tactical fit.

The interest is understood to pre-date Pochettino's appointment at Old Trafford, which is significant. Recruitment work had already been undertaken on Bassey, and the arrival of the Argentine has only strengthened that position. The key detail from the report is that the Nigeria international is regarded as a "very good fit" for the new head coach's system.

Calvin Bassey seen as strong tactical fit

That phrase matters. Pochettino's sides have long been associated with an aggressive defensive line, mobility across the back line and the ability to recover quickly in transition. In that context, Bassey's athletic profile stands out. He is quick, physically dominant and comfortable defending larger spaces, attributes that are increasingly non-negotiable for elite teams trying to play on the front foot.

There is also a practical element to United's thinking. Bassey can operate as a left-sided centre-back and at left-back, which gives the club what the report describes as a "double reason" to consider a deal. That versatility inevitably sharpens the focus on the wider balance of the squad, particularly given the uncertainty around Luke Shaw's contract situation.

Sources cited in the report state Bassey is viewed internally as a "very good fit" and, crucially, that he "would be more than open to the prospect of a move to Old Trafford". For any club planning a major January move, alignment on profile and player willingness is a major starting point.

Fulham contract stance could shape January window

United's interest does not automatically make this straightforward. Fulham retain a degree of control over the situation. Bassey is approaching the final months of his deal, but the west London club hold an option to extend. The report states they have already indicated an intention to trigger that option if fresh contract terms cannot be agreed.

Even so, the position appears far from fully settled. Alvaro Arbeloa is said to want Bassey to stay, yet talks over an extension "have not progressed as hoped". That has left his camp attentive to developments, with outside interest beginning to build.

It is in that context that United are prepared to explore whether Fulham's stance can be tested in the January market. Clubs do not move aggressively in winter without conviction, and this is a case where the tactical argument and the market opportunity may be converging.

Manchester United face £40m-plus Calvin Bassey valuation

The obvious complication is price. TeamTalk reports that a fee "in excess of £40million" would likely be required, with Fulham potentially seeking close to £50million before considering a sale. That is a substantial figure for a January deal and would represent a major decision for United, particularly with other areas of the squad also requiring attention.

For Fulham, a sale at that level would carry historic significance, surpassing the £43.5million received from Al-Hilal for Aleksandar Mitrovic in 2023. That context helps explain why they are under no pressure to soften their position quickly.

United are understood to want a new left-sided central defender regardless of any eventual call on Lisandro Martinez, whose future remains open according to the report. Bassey is one of several names under assessment, alongside Jarrad Branthwaite, Nathan Collins and Castello Lukeba, but there is a sense that his combination of suitability, versatility and openness to the move has elevated him within the process.

If this report is accurate, the logic is easy to follow. The biggest appeal with Bassey is that he seems to answer more than one question at once. Manchester United need speed in defence, more security in wide areas and better protection against transitions. A player comfortable at left centre-back and left-back immediately improves the options available.

The valuation is the sticking point. Paying more than £40m in January for a defender who is highly rated but not yet universally viewed among the very top bracket feels like a serious gamble. Fulham would be well within their rights to demand it, especially with his physical tools and Premier League experience, but United have been here before with expensive deals that made sense on paper and looked far less convincing later on.

Still, there is something encouraging about the profile. This sounds like a move driven by system fit rather than reputation. That is how recruitment should look. If Pochettino wants defenders who can hold a high line and recover fast, then Bassey ticks obvious boxes. The mention that he is "more than open to the prospect of a move to Old Trafford" also suggests this would not require selling a dream to a reluctant target.

The concern is whether United can get this done at the right number. If the fee moves towards £50m, alternatives such as Branthwaite or Lukeba may start to look more attractive. Even so, Bassey feels like one to watch because the need, the style and the player profile all appear aligned.

articles.body:
Senny Mayulu is a real talent and seems like a lovely kid. He's been speaking about making his France debut this week.

If you enjoy PSG Talk coverage and want to see more of it, add us as a preferred source on Google to make us a favourite and see more of our content.

Senny Mayulu has been the star of this international break, from a PSG point of view.

He was starting regularly for the Parisians before the break, and continued that run with a first call up for France's senior team, then a debut for Les Bleus against Italy this week.

But Mayulu was clear on who the credit should really go to: Luis Enrique.

Mayulu credits coach for impressive start to senior career

Senny Mayulu. (Photo by Catherine Steenkeste/Getty Images for Qatar Airways)

"He's my first coach, he helped me enormously to make the leap from youth player to professional. He helped me progress and he still does so every day in Ligue 1," Mayulu said in quotes picked up by FootMercato.

"I'm finding it hard to believe, it all happened so fast. It was my first season as a pro, and we immediately won the Champions League. We did it again the following year. After that, you get a taste for it and you want to win it all the time. A third Champions League title? The coach keeps us hungry for more, despite having already won the two. We're still working every day towards it."

Fabian Ruiz finished tenth in the Ballon d'Or and thinks he should have done even better, given his accomplishments this year.

Senior PSG officials are using this international break as a chance to get contract talks going with several key players.

France are back in action on Sunday, and ahead of the game Zinezine Zidane has been praising Desire Doue.

articles.title: Hungary boss confirms Dominik Szoboszlai fitness as Liverpool prepare for Manchester United
articles.summary: Hungary manager Marco Rossi has addressed Dominik Szoboszlai's fitness ahead of Liverpool's highly anticipated Premier League game against Manchester United...
articles.body:
Hungary manager Marco Rossi has confirmed that Dominik Szoboszlai is healthy and not dealing with any injury concerns.

Szoboszlai was substituted during Liverpool's 3-1 victory over Crystal Palace prior to the international break. The Reds midfielder sustained a minor knee issue during the triumph at Selhurst Park, requiring heavy strapping to make it to the 69th minute, yet still traveled for international duty with Hungary.

Concerns resurfaced, however, ahead of Hungary's game against Georgia on Saturday. Szoboszlai featured and registered an assist in the 2-0 victory in Tbilisi, but admitted post-match that he had contemplated withdrawing during the warm-up.

"I came today with a workout and a half in my legs," he said via The Mirror . "During the warm-up I was close to saying no, because I felt my leg on one of the shots. But if I've come this far, I won't let the team down. I went as best I could, trying to give my best."

Szoboszlai remains a pivotal figure for Liverpool, who welcome Manchester United to Anfield on Sunday following the international break. Reds boss Andoni Iraola will be anxious to have his influential midfielder return unharmed after Hungary's last UEFA Nations League group stage fixture against Northern Ireland in Budapest on Tuesday.

Hungary manager Rossi remains adamant that Szoboszlai is fully fit. "Have you noticed problems in the previous matches? In Georgia?" he said in his pre-match press conference on Monday. "I didn't see any problem in Dominik. He played like he is usually going to play so for us there is no problem, he is available.

"I don't think the situation is affecting him too much and you can see clearly by the performance. I don't think we have anything to complain about his performance in Georgia."

To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE

Tension has emerged between Hungary and Liverpool regarding Szoboszlai, with Iraola making his position clear that he wanted the 26-year-old to sit out this round of Nations League fixtures due to the knee issue.

"The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games. Last time, we lost three very important players," he said. "It's the last thing we need, so I hope he can take care of it. I think he extended a little bit the knee, he was fine, but not 100 percent.

"So he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not, but also hope that it doesn't happen like the other international break when we lost Alex [Alexander Isak], Cody [Gakpo], Dom. So, touch wood, we are in a better place in two weeks."

Across all competitions for Liverpool this season, Szoboszlai has registered three goals and one assist in 11 appearances.

articles.title: UVA basketball climbs to No. 4 in latest AP Poll
articles.summary: The ’Hoos enter the top four after their comeback win at Maryland.
articles.body:
The Virginia Cavaliers (5-0, 0-0 ACC), fresh off their come-from-behind four-point win over Maryland on Friday evening, rose two spots to No. 4 in this week's AP Poll, released Monday afternoon.

At No. 4, the 'Hoos have now entered the AP Poll's top five for the first time since appearing at No. 2 on December 12, 2022, which marked the fourth and final week that UVA was inside the top five during the 2022-23 season.

Monday's ascension in the polls comes after Virginia overcame an 11-point halftime deficit inside the Xfinity Center on Friday evening against former ACC rival Maryland. In what was the 186 th edition of the all-time series against the Terrapins, Sam Lewis erupted for a career-high 28 points as the 'Hoos shot 76.9% from the floor in the second half to storm back and silence a sold-out Maryland crowd.

The win in College Park completed a 2-0 week for Ryan Odom's squad after Virginia bested Bucknell, 95-61, at home inside John Paul Jones Arena on Tuesday night.

Aside from the 'Hoos, the ACC suffered a rough week in the rankings. Former No. 2 Duke dropped three spots to No. 5 following a loss to Michigan State in Tuesday night's Champions Classic, while former No. 10 Louisville plummeted 13 spots to No. 23 after a 20-point road loss at Memphis. No. 17 Miami, the conference's only other ranked team, stood pat after a pair of buy-game wins.

At the top of the rankings, No. 1 Florida held on to the top spot after a nine-point road win over in-state rival Florida State on Tuesday; No. 2 Michigan State jumped up three spots after taking down the Blue Devils; and No. 3 UConn climbed one spot to round out the top three.

The fourth-ranked 'Hoos, who enter the week at No. 6 in Bart Torvik's T-Rankings and No. 12 at KenPom, will return home for a pair of weeknight matchups inside JPJ with Old Dominion (Tuesday at 9 PM) and Loyola MD (Friday at 7 PM).

articles.title: England Under-21s 3-2 France Under-21s: Max Dowman becomes Three Lions' youngest ever U21 scorer with dramatic winner
articles.summary: Max Dowman becomes England Under-21s youngest-ever goalscorer aged 16 with an 89th-minute winner in a 3-2 win over France; Lee Carsley's side strode into a 2-0 lead through Mikey Moore and Divin Mubama but conceded twice in five minutes past the 80th-minute, before Dowman won it
articles.body:
The 16-year-old Arsenal prodigy became England's youngest Under-21s player last week in the defeat to Portugal - but made even more history by popping up with an 89th-minute winner on his second appearance, as he played the entire game.

At 16 years and 320 days old, Dowman is the youngest-ever goalscorer for England at this level. The previous record was held by current England men's senior star Jude Bellingham - who broke the record aged 17 years and 67 days against Kosovo in September 2020.

"We see how good on the ball he is but he was outstanding off the ball," said England U21s boss Lee Carsley. "You have to keep reminding yourself about his age.

"There's a lot of expectation around him and he seems to handle that so well. It's important we keep supporting him and he develops at his own pace. It's so important he enjoys his football.

"Obviously, all the players in the squad are under pressure from their clubs and the expectation that surrounds them, so as much as we can we have to make that as easy as we can."

England endured a lacklustre evening three days ago on Dowman's debut against Portugal but made a lightning start this time around as Mikey Moore gave England an early lead on his first under-21s start before Divin Mubama doubled their lead.

The Young Lions were comfortable but Tommy Setford made a second mistake in as many games which allowed France to pull a goal back after he let Giovani Versini's cross slip through his fingers before the Frenchman equalised in style moments later.

Carsley had handed a first start to promising Arsenal youngster Dowman and he proved to be the hero who tapped in to give England the win at only 16 years old.

England got off to the perfect start and went a goal to the good after some great work from Ethan Nwaneri down the left allowed him to feed it into Moore, who tucked expertly beyond Mathieu Patouillet.

The Young Lions doubled their advantage in the 29th minute and Nwaneri once again provided the assist by lifting a high ball onto the head of Mubama who nodded back across goal to make it 2-0.

France did not threaten in the first half but started the second period a lot more menacingly. Dayann Methalie found himself with space inside the box but fired wide with their best chance of the game so far.

England almost made it three down the other end when Nwaneri was denied by the diving save of Patouille only for the ball to come back out to the Borussia Dortmund loanee, who then saw his second effort cleared off the line by Nathan Zeze.

Setford's mistake gave Portugal the win on Friday, and he was once again at fault when Versini's rather untroubling cross slipped through his fingers to make it 2-1.

But there was nothing Setford could do about the second when Versini let fly from range with an effort that flew into the back of the net.

However, England re-established their lead four minutes later when Harrison Armstrong fed it to Dowman, who was unmarked inside the box to tap into an empty net for a history-making strike.

articles.title: CFP Playoff Bracket, Scenarios and Bowl Projections After 2026-27 Week 12 AP Rankings
articles.summary: Change was hard to find in the Week 12 AP Top 25.
articles.body:
Change was hard to find in the Week 12 AP Top 25.

The Georgia Bulldogs, Utah Utes, Notre Dame Fighting Irish, UCLA Bruins and Miami Hurricanes are the top five in that order for the second straight week.

In fact, only one change was made inside the top 10, as the Wake Forest Demon Deacons moved up to No. 10 in place of the Texas Tech Red Raiders.

There were plenty of multi-spot movers in the second half of the poll. The Boise State Broncos were one of the most notable movers up to No. 15, seven spots ahead of the next-best Group of Six school, the Liberty Flames.

Wake Forest Jumps Texas Tech to Claim No. 10

The AP voters delivered a small statement on Monday with Wake Forest jumping Texas Tech to grab the final spot in the top 10.

That's a significant jump because we're using the No. 11 spot in the AP poll as the cutoff line for College Football Playoff teams.

The switch between Nos. 10 and 11 makes Texas Tech potentially vulnerable to make the 12-team playoff field.

The CFB Playoff rankings come out on Tuesday night. That's when we'll understand what the selection committee thinks of Wake Forest and Texas Tech.

Wake is more than deserving of a spot in the top 10. It's blown through most of its ACC schedule, including a road blowout of the SMU Mustangs in Week 11.

The Demon Deacons are the ACC's best hope to put two teams into the playoff.

They are expected to face Miami in a rematch from September in the ACC Championship Game. The selection committee's been lenient with punishment for losing a conference championship game, so it's good news for Wake, at least for now, that it's a top-10 team.

Boise State moved inside the top 15 in Monday's poll.

The Broncos have been the favorite to earn the Group of Six's automatic bid to the CFB Playoff for most of the season.

Boise slowly moved up the rankings after every win. It jumped two spots on Monday following its ninth win of the campaign.

Only a few games stand between Boise and the CFB Playoff. It is expected to win the Pac-12 and enter as the No. 12 seed in the bracket.

The fact that Boise sits at No. 15 is significant, though, because it shows just how much quality the Broncos have on their roster.

Boise won't be like other previous G6 representatives that fail to compete in the playoff. It has a real chance to be competitive with whomever it faces in the opening round.

If Boise suffers an upset, the Liberty Flames appear to be the next team up. The Conference USA side entered the AP poll at No. 22.

Oregon, Ohio State Lingering Outside Top 12

The Oregon Ducks and Ohio State Buckeyes aren't completely out of the CFB Playoff conversation yet.

Oregon moved up four spots to No. 14 on Monday, while Ohio State checked in at No. 16.

The pair of preseason top-10 teams sit behind the Iowa Hawkeyes at No. 13 as the three contenders to earn a third Big Ten spot in the CFB Playoff alongside UCLA and the Indiana Hoosiers.

Oregon plays the Michigan State Spartans and Washington Huskies to close out the regular season. It could finish 9-3 with a trio of Top 25 victories.

Ohio State visits the Nebraska Cornhuskers and then plays the Michigan Wolverines in its final two games. It could be sitting at 9-3 with wins over Iowa and Indiana and losses to Oregon and Texas.

Both teams need help to reach the top 11, but in a season where chaos has reigned supreme for weeks on end, you can never say never about the playoff potential of the Ducks and Buckeyes.

There is a scenario in which Oregon, Iowa and Ohio State are the three teams fighting for the last at-large bid. How the selection committee untangles that mess will be fascinating to see if it happens.

articles.title: Wales vs Portugal: No Cristiano Ronaldo for the visitors as Craig Bellamy's side have a free hit in final Nations League encounter
articles.summary: Wales take on Portugal in the Nations League on Tuesday, with the visitors without Cristiano Ronaldo in Cardiff after his retirement; Ben Davies is pretty pleased the legendary forward is not in the Portugal squad - with Craig Bellamy unmoved by the whole saga
articles.body:
Mark the date, November 17, 2026 - it could have been the last time to see Cristiano Ronaldo play on UK soil.

A mouthwatering occasion to witness one of the greats of the game as the curtain slowly falls on his illustrious international career and also see just how far Wales are progressing after a full campaign in League A of the Nations League, a full campaign among the heavyweights of European football.

As we all know, that's not how it's panned out! After Ronaldo's appearance against Wales in Lisbon at the start of the Nations League, he's not featured since - and he's now called time on his Portugal career amid some controversy.

Even though Ronaldo's not here in Wales and the ending of his Portugal days were perhaps not the best scripted, he'll certainly be missed by many. Wales manager Craig Bellamy for one: "As soon as he retires then suddenly like, it's all hell breaks loose!

"He is one of the best players that has ever played the game. We are all going to miss him. Now, he's still playing club football, so we still get little bits to watch him.

"So just be grateful you got to see an incredible talent that you can call yours, and this is me speaking to Portuguese people. But I'm grateful that we got to see the longevity of a true great, who's had one of the biggest impacts in football in general and will go on to have a big impact by just the young kids who watch him.

"I feel it's like stop the talking now. Just celebrate. Celebrate. I'm grateful I got to see him and I'm grateful I got to coach against him as well."

Wales captain Ben Davies offered a wry smile and an alternative view of Ronaldo's retirement, from an opposition player's perspective: "Any game where you probably don't play against Cristiano Ronaldo, I think it's sometimes better for you…" That's Davies at his most understated!

He added: "You're not too concerned of what he can do to you on that day, he's a world-class player. It's been an honour and a privilege to share the pitch with him because of what he's done in the game. We were lucky to do that in Lisbon, but there won't be too many players in Wales complaining that he's not going to be there."

Despite the Wales-Portugal fixture having implications for both countries, more questions were asked about Ronaldo than perhaps most others. Welsh, British and Portuguese reporters were all guilty at some point of asking media questions about the missing No 7.

Take away the circus that followed and still follows Ronaldo, so many Wales fans thought about buying a ticket and coming along to watch Ronaldo strut his stuff and to also show their appreciation, that it's actually difficult to ignore Ronaldo's absence from their perspective.

Fans pay good money to watch elite sport and many had hoped a farewell to Ronaldo was part of the entrance fee. A great shame for nigh on 35,000 inside the Cardiff City Stadium on Tuesday night.

What the crowd will get though is a Portugal side packed with talent - the quality and depth of their squad on paper is ridiculous.

But it's a squad that has come to Cardiff slightly reeling from a very unexpected home thrashing at the hands of Denmark who beat them 4-1 at the weekend.

Is this what Portugal will be like without Ronaldo? I doubt it… but Wales have a free shot at Portugal, their League A campaign has only mustered one win, but bar a drab home game against Denmark, Bellamy's side have gone toe to toe with Portugal and Norway.

There have been "moments" as Bellamy ruefully alluded to in all matches where Wales have produced quality and consistency beyond their opponents. It's brought a victory over Norway, but in the other four games Wales have just been short. Short, but at least trying.

Even the most ardent Wales supporter who is not a "Bellamy" fans (and there a few) can't talk away some plain stats. Wales have enjoyed decent possession in all their League A games and create chances - 12 against Norway last Saturday. Perhaps one link missing is an out and out goalscorer where chances created and shots at goal actually turn into 'goals'.

For Bellamy this League A campaign has been fruitful IF you can look beyond the short term: "You want to be exposed to the profile of teams we've been exposed to. It's beyond motivating to play these teams and even the moments that don't go your way, you learn, you know? Like that killer moment.

"You can't get away with anything, can you? At the moment, we've got in, we're side-netting (not the goal), so it's the difference. I thought we definitely brought a good version of ourselves to these games, we've definitely been competitive in these games and I expect us to be competitive, but it's just final moments, those final details.

"Are we creating opportunities to score? Well, xG is higher than what we're converging so that's telling you we're creating big opportunities.

"They're the moments that can turn what you feel is a good performance into actually coming away and winning these type of games and I believe the best way you're able to do that is by playing against them on a regular basis, by being in that position.

"So yeah, we're desperate to stay in Group A. We want to stay in this league, it motivates us a lot to stay in this league."

Bellamy's Wales will finish bottom of their group, but their record is better than many other teams in League A such as Czech Republic, Serbia and Turkey so they will not be automatically relegated.

A play-off awaits Wales next March against a League B runner-up. Wales will take that and fancy their chances especially with the home leg second.

With Euro 2028 the longer term aim, remaining in League A the medium term aim, the short term is to do a Wales 'rugby'.

Defy the pundits and 'superior' opposition and create a result and performance that many people talk about for years to come and say to one another; "I was there… even if Ronaldo wasn't."

articles.title: Cazorla pide tiempo para Raúl en el Oviedo: “Tiene un conocimiento increíble”
articles.standfirst: El asturiano destaca la cercanía del técnico y cuenta que, por lo que le trasladan sus compañeros, el vestuario está contento con el trabajo diario
articles.summary: El asturiano destaca la cercanía del técnico y cuenta que, por lo que le trasladan sus compañeros, el vestuario está contento con el trabajo diario
articles.body: Santi Cazorla pide tiempo para Raúl González Blanco en el Real Oviedo. El asturiano considera que el nuevo entrenador tiene las condiciones para sacar adelante al equipo y se apoya en lo que le cuentan desde el vestuario. “Tiene un conocimiento increíble, es una persona muy cercana”, dijo Cazorla, que atendió a los medios antes de la gala del diario Sport. Raúl se estrenó con una derrota ante el Girona y afrontará su segundo partido en el banquillo azul el domingo en Córdoba. Cazorla recordó que el técnico acaba de llegar y defendió que necesita margen para trabajar con la plantilla. “Lleva pocos días en el cargo y va a necesitar un poco de tiempo para adaptarse al equipo”, explicó. Por lo que ha hablado con sus compañeros, añadió, “están todos muy contentos en el día a día con él”. Cazorla contó también de dónde viene su trato con el exentrenador del Castilla. “Tengo una gran amistad con él”, señaló. Los dos han coincidido en los últimos meses porque sus hijos juegan juntos en el filial del Real Oviedo. El asturiano le deseó suerte en el banquillo y, preguntado por su capacidad para dirigir al equipo, sostuvo que “es la persona idónea”. Cazorla también repasó la actualidad de la selección española. “No hay que dramatizar. No siempre se puede ganar”, dijo antes de reivindicar el nivel del equipo. Sobre Lamine Yamal, al que le pidieron comparar con el Messi de sus primeros años, prefirió centrarse en lo que ya está mostrando el azulgrana y lo situó como el futbolista con mayor proyección del momento. El asturiano también confía en que Vinícius recupere su mejor nivel por la capacidad que tiene para marcar diferencias en el Real Madrid. Habló en términos parecidos de Frenkie de Jong, con el que se ha enfrentado sobre el césped, y deseó que las lesiones le permitan tener continuidad en el Barcelona. De Xavi Hernández, con quien coincidió en Qatar, dijo que le considera “un entrenador de primer nivel”.

articles.title: Vitor Matos: Strasbourg target Swansea City head coach
articles.summary: Vitor Matos has emerged as a target for French top-flight club Strasbourg who could soon part ways with Hugo Oliveira.
articles.body:
Swansea City look to be facing a fight to hold on to Vitor Matos amid serious interest in their head coach from French top-flight club Strasbourg.

Matos is under contract at Swansea until 2030, meaning the Championship side would be due significant compensation should he be lured away.

But that has not stopped Strasbourg targeting the 38-year-old Portuguese, who is due to celebrate a year in charge at Swansea later this month.

Matos' fellow countryman Hugo Oliveira is the current Strasbourg boss, but is under pressure after a run of five defeats in six matches.

Oliveira has managed only three wins in 10 league games since succeeding Gary O'Neil - who left to become Ipswich Town boss – in July.

O'Neil led Strasbourg to an eighth-place finish last season, but they are currently 13th in Ligue 1, only two points above the relegation zone.

Strasbourg are a sister club of Premier League side Chelsea.

Matos has turned Swansea from potential relegation contenders to promotion hopefuls since taking charge, with the club 20th in the Championship when he took over last November.

The Swans finished 11th last season and have made further strides in the first third of this campaign.

Matos' team have been among the early-season pacesetters in the second tier, enjoying two spells on top of the table, but their form has dipped in recent weeks.

Swansea have suffered four defeats in their past five matches, though they remain only three points off top spot going into Saturday's home game against West Bromwich Albion.

Matos was touted as a contender to take charge at Crystal Palace earlier this season - the Eagles have since appointed Thomas Frank - while he has also been linked with a return to Portugal on the back of his impact with the Swans.

Latest Swansea City news, analysis and fan views

Listen to the latest Swansea City interviews, news and discussion on BBC Sounds

When asked in October about the Palace links, Matos said: "I'm Swansea manager. I love being here, love my players, love the staff, so my focus is always on the next game and what we can do better."

In an interview last week, Swansea chief executive Tom Gorringe acknowledged that Matos' impact will not have gone unnoticed at other clubs, though he played down the idea of the former Liverpool coach having his head turned.

"The reality is there'll always be interest in anyone performing well in any role on and off the pitch," Gorringe said.

"That's one of the outcomes of being successful - we're aware of that.

"[But] we're all quite happy. We've all agreed to go on this journey together and we hope that Vitor is here a long time."

After West Brom visit, Swansea go to second-placed Middlesbrough next Tuesday before Cardiff City make the short trip west for the first south Wales derby in two seasons on Sunday, 29 November.

articles.title: Declan Rice contract: Arsenal midfielder verbally agrees new deal with the Premier League champions
articles.summary: Declan Rice has just over 18 months left on his existing contract, with a further year's option in Arsenal's favour; the Premier League champions want to bring him in line with the club's top earner, Bukayo Saka; Rice admitted on England duty that he is close to a new agreement
articles.body:
Sky Sports News has been told his new deal will bring him in line with Bukayo Saka, who is the highest-paid player at the Emirates.

Rice and his representatives have been in negotiations for several months, with the club keen to tie down one of their most important players, even though he still has 18 months left on his existing contract, with a further year's option in the club's favour.

Rice was named Arsenal's Player of the Year last season when they won the Premier League title and this new deal will take him into his early 30s.

The 27-year-old joined Arsenal from West Ham for a club record £105m in 2023. He's gone on to be a key member of Mikel Arteta's leadership group, and someone who the Spanish coach has built his team around.

Speaking on Saturday ahead of England's final Nations League group game in Spain, Rice confirmed that he was close to an agreement.

"I'm a player that always sets myself targets, always pushes for more. I've always been stable in the clubs I'm at. The new contract is hopefully on the horizon soon.

"I'm extremely lucky I'm at a club like Arsenal where the manager shows me so much trust. I've so many team-mates who put so much energy and effort into me. I'm extremely lucky that I don't have to worry about that stuff. It makes playing football a lot easier."

Analysis: Best in the league? Rice is the complete midfielder

Arsenal are not just tying down Declan Rice - one of their most important players - to a bumper new deal, they are tying down arguably the Premier League's best player into his remaining peak years.

And this season is the best version we've ever seen from Rice.

The England midfielder has started the campaign on fire and tops the Premier League assist charts at the moment with five - all of them from open play.

But this creative spark from Rice has come despite the Arsenal man playing a deeper role in Mikel Arteta's set-up. A sitting midfielder, yes - but still as attacking as ever.

No midfielder in the Premier League has made more final third passes or passes through the lines than Rice this season.

His number of final third entries has nearly doubled compared to two seasons ago. And his recent goal for Arsenal against Bayern Munich in the Champions League summed up how he is influencing the top end of the pitch a lot more.

That goal cancelled out Harry Kane's strike for Bayern. Rice is Arsenal's superstar equivalent.

Rice can do everything in midfield for Arsenal. He can hurt teams by running through them, or passing through the lines. He can score, as well as create. He can damage from open play, or from his deadly delivery from corners and free-kicks. He is the complete midfielder.

Odegaard yet to begin new Arsenal contract talks

Meanwhile, another huge figure in the Arsenal starting XI - captain Martin Odegaard - has said he has not yet begun negotiations over a new contract, even though his current deal expires at the same time as Rice's.

Speaking while on international duty with Norway, the Arsenal captain said: "I'm happy and hope I can be there for a long time to come, but so far we haven't started on that.

"There is no stress about it. I am where I am, and I am super happy with it. Things are going well, and it is not something I am stressed about. As I said, I want to be there for a long time to come. I am enjoying myself a lot."

articles.title: Switzerland 4-0 Scotland: Andy Robertson breaks caps record as Scots fall to heavy Nations League defeat
articles.summary: Match report as Scotland lose to Switzerland in their final Nations League Group B1 match; Lewis Ferguson's own-goal put the hosts ahead; Winsley Boteli, Alvyn Sanches and Zeki Amdouni scored in the second half; Scotland will remain in League B for the next Nations League tournament
articles.body:
On the night he became the men's record appearance holder with 103 caps, Sebastien Pocognoli came under pressure with a bruising 4-0 defeat in St Gallen.

"That cannot happen in international football," he told BBC Scotland after the match.

"I don't think you've got time in international football, you have to do it. These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden, who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.

"We don't have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up.

"We have a long break now to March, which is not a good thing, and it is going to be a tough one to swallow."

The Scots were comfortable against the much-changed Group B1 winners until the 22nd minute when midfielder Lewis Ferguson put through his own goal.

The unforced error deflated the visitors, who lost wing-back Aaron Hickey to injury before the break, and there was more damage in the 47th minute when Samuel Ballet's drive was touched in by Winsley Boteli before Alvyn Sanches hammered in a third just four minutes later, with substitute Zeki Amdouni adding a late fourth.

The Scots finished third in the group behind Switzerland and Slovenia, with seven points from 18, missing out on a promotion play-off spot next year and a more favourable seeding for the European Championship qualifying draw next month.

The Belgian boss' first campaign as Steve Clarke's successor has been underwhelming to say the least with just two wins - both against bottom side North Macedonia - from six fixtures and Pocognoli now finds himself under the spotlight just months into his tenure.

The key moments from Berit Sitterstadion

2: SAVE! A comfortable save for Angus Gunn but Isaac Schmidt is given too much time to get a shot away. An early warning.

17: CHANCE! John McGinn hooks the ball over the bar as Scotland continue to pile on the pressure.

22: GOAL SWITZERLAND! Disaster for Scotland as Lewis Ferguson sticks out his leg and sends the ball into his own net.

24: CLOSE! Almost an equaliser from Aaron Hickey. He gets his head to Andy Robertson's cross, but it's just past the post.

36: INJURY! Hickey pulls up holding his hamstring and his night is over.

42: CHANCE! Nathan Patterson sends the ball in to McGinn but he heads straight at the goalkeeper. An opportunity missed.

44: CHANCE! That should be a second for Switzerland! Adrian Bajrami gets on the end of the cross but somehow heads the ball well off target.

47: GOAL SWITZERLAND! Samuel Ballet plays a one-two with Remo Freuler, and Winsley Boteli gets the last touch to put the Swiss two up.

51: GOAL SWITZERLAND! Alvyn Sanches gets on the end of a ball from Boteli and fires across Gunn and into the net.

66: SAVE! Gunn pulls off a save to deny Ballet a fourth for the hosts and Luke Graham is there to block Zeki Amdouni's follow-up effort.

72: OVER! Scott McTominay gets on the end of Kieran Tierney's cross and somehow blasts it over the bar.

85: SUB! Kristi Montgomery replaces Ferguson as he makes his Scotland debut.

89: GOAL SWITZERLAND! Amdouni's shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection off Graham as it goes past Gunn.

Almost a year on from the elation of Scotland beating Denmark to reach the World Cup, it now looks like a struggle to reach Euro 2028.

Scotland will be in Pot 3 when the draw is made next month, and there is a lot of improvement needed before the qualifying campaign then kicks off in March.

In his first six games as Steve Clarke's successor, Sebastien Pocognoli has won just two. Both against North Macedonia.

They had a decent first 20 minutes in St Gallen, but this was not Switzerland's best team.

Murat Yakin was without Granit Xhaka, Dan Ndoye, Manuel Akanji and Johan Manzambi and they still made it look easy against the Scots who managed just one shot on target. A tame one.

How much time should the new Scotland head coach bet given? Following the man who led the nation to three major tournaments was always going to be a hard act to follow, but the team appears to have regressed.

Pocognoli positive about Scotland's future

Scotland head coach Sebastien Pocognoli speaking to BBC Scotland:

"The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game, if I'm really honest and objective.

"I think we had some very good moments in the game, we started the game like we wanted, aggressive away from home.

"I think if we were in confidence, we would not produce the moments we produce in the game.

"I think we create good moments on the ball, on pure bravery decisions to play forward through the lines or the pressure.

"We create chances also for pressing, sometimes we should have to manage better the transition from pressing, but it is all the things we want to see.

"So the next step is to have the quality to just finish this action, and the more we have games together, the more we will try to fix these things.

"We have a lot of good response from this camp and it's good for the future as well."

Robertson: 'That can't happen, we've got to step up'

Scotland captain Andy Robertson speaking to BBC Scotland:

"First half we were in the game but lost a stupid goal. But I thought we had chances and should have made it one each at half-time.

"We talked about it at half-time, we told ourselves to keep going and the time you get to 50 minutes, you're 3-0 down? That cannot happen in international football.

"That's what happened tonight. We were playing against a good team. But while we were in the game in the first half, you have to do it for 90 minutes. Then you're 3-0 down, it's a tough place to come and that. A really tough night for us."

articles.title: Germany thrash Netherlands to book quarterfinal spot
articles.summary: Jurgen Klopp’s side outclasses the Dutch 5-0 in Berlin to secure top spot in UEFA Nations League Group A2.
articles.body:
An impressive Germany swept aside off-colour Netherlands 5-0 in Berlin to pip the Dutch to first place in UEFA Nations League Group A2.

Germany needed a win to stand a chance of reaching the quarterfinals, starting the night in third place behind Greece, who had won 1-0 in Germany in September, by virtue of their head-to-head record.

Jurgen Klopp’s side produced a fine attacking display to inflict the heaviest defeat on the Dutch in 67 years, as Xavi Hernandez’s side looked very ragged as they shipped four goals in 17 second-half minutes.

Greece’s win over Serbia left the top three sides level on 11 points, but Germany took the top spot on head-to-head while the Dutch finished second, qualifying for the last eight on goal difference thanks largely to their 7-0 win over Greece on Friday.

After a quiet opening 20 minutes, Kai Havertz headed straight at keeper Bart Verbruggen from a Joshua Kimmich free-kick, while Donyell Malen headed a Cody Gakpo cross from the left of the area over the bar from close range soon after.

Berlin-born Derry Scherhant fired a half-volley against the outside of the Dutch post on 32 minutes after collecting a cross from the right byline, but it turned out to be a range-finder as Scherhant scored his first international goal from a similar position on 44 minutes. After cutting in from the left of the area and working space, he flashed an unstoppable shot past Verbruggen and into the far top corner.

Scherhant almost grabbed his second a minute after the interval as he jinked and bundled his way through on goal on the left of the area only to lash a left-footed effort over the bar with only Verbruggen to beat.

Denzel Dumfries headed over the bar at the other end after running onto a bouncing cross at the back post after ghosting past Scherhant on 48 minutes. Meanwhile, the lively Brajan Gruda came close to a spectacular second at the other end after some neat control and cutting in from the right before flashing a shot past the upright from the edge of the Dutch box.

Soon after, Gakpo tested ter Stegen with a low strike from outside the box, but Germany made him pay as Florian Wirtz doubled the lead with a stunning strike into the top corner from the edge of the D with his left foot on the hour.

Nico Schlotterbeck glanced home a header from Gruda’s curling free-kick from the left within five minutes to make it 3-0, and the fourth arrived soon after as Gruda was allowed to glide into the area on the right and get to the byline before dinking the ball back into the middle for the unmarked Wirtz to lash home his second goal with a volley off the underside of the bar.

Gruda nearly added a goal to his two assists as his rising shot was stopped by Verbruggen after another silky run, but the 22-year-old eventually marked his second cap with his second international goal on 77 minutes when he fired home the rebound after Scherhant’s shot came back off the inside of the post.

It led to Verbruggen calling an impromptu huddle outside his area as the visitors sought to end their misery, and they saw the game out without further alarm.

Germany will be seeded in Friday’s draw for the last eight, which will be contested over two legs in March.

articles.title: Philip Rivers Talks Emotional NC State Return in Video After Legendary Quarterback Named HC
articles.summary: Philip Rivers was unveiled as NC State's new head coach on Monday and became emotional while speaking about what it meant to return to his alma mater.
articles.body:
Philip Rivers was unveiled as NC State's new head coach on Monday and became emotional while speaking about what it meant to return to his alma mater.

"For me, at 44 and soon to be 45..." Rivers said before pausing to compose himself. "I do feel like we all have many gifts. And I do feel like god has given me the gift to serve and impact through this game. And I've got a lot still to give. And there ain't no better place, or any place that I would really want to give it, besides right here at NC State."

Rivers played quarterback for NC State (2000-03) before a long and successful NFL career that included eight Pro Bowl berths in stints with the San Diego/Los Angeles Chargers (2004-19) and the Indianapolis Colts (2020; 2025).

He transitioned to coaching after his playing career, leading St. Michael Catholic High School to the Alabama state semifinals in 2024 and 2025. And now he'll be replacing Dave Doeren, who was fired on Oct. 24.

"I gave it everything I had here as a player for 51 games and I will give it everything I have as the coach," Rivers told reporters on Friday. "There's no denying that this is going to take hard work, but we're not scared of hard. I look forward to getting after it every single day with an unbelievable coaching staff and a group of players who are dedicated to relentlessly pursuing victory."

articles.title: Andy Robertson: Scotland captain breaks national appearance record by winning 103rd senior cap vs Switzerland
articles.summary: Andy Robertson became Scotland's most-capped men's player with start against Switzerland in Nations League; he passed Kenny Dalglish's record of 102 caps; Robertson on Sir Kenny: "I don't want to forget and I don't want people to forget how important this man has been for our country."
articles.body:
The Scotland captain made his 103rd appearance for the national side in Monday's 4-0 defeat to Switzerland in the Nations League.

He has bypassed the record set by Dalglish, who earned 102 caps between 1971 and 1986.

Before hitting the milestone, Robertson insisted he will always regard Dalglish as "the greatest" .

"We've had so many great players for Scotland, but for me Kenny will always stand on top and I don't think that will change," the 32-year-old said.

"I don't want to forget and I don't want people to forget how important this man has been for our country."

Asked about what he told Robertson before the game, Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli said: "I just tell him that he has to enjoy it and after it's just a bonus for the future. So he needs to enjoy, to play with freedom.

"He has a lot of experience, so I don't need to tell him, but again, we are really proud of what we are living together with him. And the best way to have a good feeling for him is to have a good game."

Scotland midfielder Lewis Ferguson added: "It's amazing. First and foremost what a person, what an unbelievable captain, what a player and what an incredible servant for Scotland.

"It's a massive achievement, he should be so proud of himself and we're all just glad to be a part of that journey."

A night to remember, but not the way he wanted

Andy Robertson spoke to BBC Scotland after the defeat in St Gallen:

"First half we were in the game but lost a stupid goal. But I thought we had chances and should have made it one each at half-time.

"We talked about it at half-time, we told ourselves to keep going and the time you get to 50 minutes, you're 3-0 down? That cannot happen in international football.

"That's what happened tonight. We were playing against a good team. But while we were in the game in the first half, you have to do it for 90 minutes. Then you're 3-0 down, it's a tough place to come and that. A really tough night for us."

"I don't think you've got time in international football, you have to do it. These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden, who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.

"We don't have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up.

"We have a long break now to March, which is not a good thing, and it is going to be a tough one to swallow."

articles.title: Sebastien Pocognoli wants patience but Scotland 'don't have time' says Andy Robertson
articles.summary: Angry captain Andy Robertson says Scotland do not have time to turn things around after a brutal 4-0 defeat by Switzerland consigns them to a third-place finish in their Nations League group.
articles.body:
Angry captain Andy Robertson says Scotland do not have time to turn things around after a brutal 4-0 defeat by Switzerland consigned them to a third-place finish in their Nations League group.

Head coach Sebastien Pocognoli - appointed as Steve Clarke's successor in August - has consistently stressed the need for patience as he tries to implement a more attack-minded style.

However, the Belgian has won just two of his first six matches in charge, both against North Macedonia, and conceded 10 goals in that time.

They collapsed worryingly easily in St Gallen against a much-changed Swiss outfit on Monday after a promising start, Bologna midfielder Lewis Ferguson putting through his own goal and early intensity gave way to indecision.

The Swiss struck twice in the early minutes of the second half to make it 3-0 and Zeki Amdouni made it four late on.

"First half, I thought we were in the game, we lost a stupid goal, but I thought we had chances and could have been 2-1 at half time," a frustrated Robertson said, on the night he surpassed Kenny Dalglish as his country's most capped men's player.

"By the time you get to 50 minutes and you're 3-0 down, that can't happen in international football.

"It is a really tough night for us. I don't think you've got time in international football, you have to do it.

"These supporters who travel everywhere, are they going to give us time? No. Are the people inside Hampden going to give us time? No. Are the people outside Hampden who are going to be critical and rightly so? No.

"We don't have time, the players do not have time, we have got to step up.

"We have a long break now to March, which is not a good thing, and it is going to be a tough one to swallow."

What's the story with Pocognoli, is it now time to go?

Pocognoli's abject Scotland beaten 4-0 in Switzerland

Robertson eclipses Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped man

'Passion and fight' lacking - should Pocognoli follow Clarke blueprint?

This was meant to be a special occasion for Robertson, but it was usurped by the debate over Pocognoli's future.

Just six games into his tenure, there are serious questions being asked over whether the former Union Saint-Gilloise and Monaco coach is capable of delivering on his promise of making Scotland easier on the eye, while delivering positive results.

Tottenham Hotspur left-back Robertson was not the only player to deliver a scathing assessment.

When asked if Scotland were on the right path, John McGinn replied: "Well, obviously the trajectory of the results means it's impossible for me to say yes."

Fellow midfielder Billy Gilmour added: "As a team we know we need to show passion and fight. We've not quite done that tonight."

Supporters are already frustrated at Pocognoli's 3-5-2 formation as they see wingers sidelined or - in the case of Ben Gannon-Doak - shoehorned into an unfamiliar wing-back role.

One man familiar with the difficulties of being the Scotland manager is former boss Craig Levein, who believes the Belgian needs to take a leaf out of his predecessor's book.

"Pocognoli is picking up where Clarke left off," Levein said on BBC Scotland. "In that situation, you need to get off to a good start. That's what the players are looking for - that you're going to make them better.

"I'd be thinking 'we need to stop losing goals'. We haven't got a potent threat, so how do we get results? As Steve recognised, you need to be hard to beat."

In contrast to his deflated players, Pocognoli put on a brave face post-match and insists he sees positive signs after his first two camps.

"The score is heavy with the 4-0, but I don't think it's a reflection of the game," he said.

"We played a good first half, we created chances, we were dominant in some moments, and we faced Switzerland with different shapes and adapted well from the first minute. We conceded from maybe one of the first chances they had.

"At the end, it's a bad feeling, the score, but I think that the players try to do their best and create moments that we want to see."

Again Pocognoli called for patience and the time which Robertson says Scotland do not have.

"The more we have games together, the more we will try to fix these things," the head coach said. "We have a lot of good response from this camp and it's good for the future as well."

But whatever Pocognoli's selling, former Scotland winger Pat Nevin isn't buying.

"If I'm ever in trouble and I need a PR man, I'm getting him because he's absolutely good at it," he said on Sportsound.

"He's certainly a glass-half-full person. You can talk away any moment and say it's just a moment, but it's four moments, five moments, six moments.

"A really horrible thing in that situation is that if I am running the SFA, I'd be asking the players what they think and just saying 'tell us the truth... are you backing us?'

"If a couple of the main ones say 'we're not sure of the decision-making' then I think it's got to that stage."

'Scotland have not played well in any game this campaign'

Fraser: Utter shambles. Embarassing. How can players who play for so called "big" clubs look like they've never seen a football before when they put on a Scotland shirt?

Matt: Six games. Six poor results. Our ranking will tank. And all Clarke's good work will be undone. It's time to admit Mulholland got it wrong. Sometimes you don't need data and metrics to see the simple solution. Poco no more.

Shirleyanne: All these comments about how rubbish we are I would like to know if they are the same people who when we play well are getting in touch praising the team?? The manager needs time, the players need time too.. Yes it's not been great but come on give them a chance and get behind them instead of moaning..

Grant: Pocognoli is the new Russell Martin, talks a good game but is actually clueless and too stubborn to admit his tactics are dire. I did say be careful what you wish for when the gaffer quit in June and this will only end one way so might as well get it done well before March. Someone should call Steve Clarke.

Brett: When you have limited resources like Scotland, you have to utilise them to good effect - take a look at what Michael O'Neil is doing with Northern Ireland, he is getting results. And you can say that Scotland has a better pool of players to choose from than Northern Ireland does, so...

articles.title: Big 12 Announces Title-Game Clinching Scenarios for Texas Tech, Utah Ahead of Week 12 Schedule
articles.summary: As the 2026 college football season heads into its final stretch, the Big 12 announced potential clinching scenarios for the 2026 Edward Jones Big 12 Football Championship game, per Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports.
articles.body:
As the 2026 college football season heads into its final stretch, the Big 12 announced potential clinching scenarios for the 2026 Edward Jones Big 12 Football Championship game, per Ross Dellenger of Yahoo Sports.

Heading into Week 12, only seven teams are still eligible for the Big 12 championship game, according to the Big 12's Tiebreaker Central page. The No. 2 Utah Utes and No. 12 Texas Tech Red Raiders are the only teams that can clinch a berth in the championship game this week.

Along with winning their respective matchups, Utah and Texas Tech would both need the No. 10 BYU Cougars to lose in order to clinch a spot.

Both teams should know the result of BYU's matchup prior to their own Week 12 games. The Cougars will travel to face the Kansas Jayhawks at noon on Saturday.

Texas Tech will host the Baylor Bears — who also remain in the hunt — on Saturday afternoon. Utah will travel to face the TCU Horned Frogs on Saturday night in Fort Worth, Texas. The Utes and Red Raiders are both favored to win their matchups on FanDuel Sportsbook .

The Utes are one of just two undefeated teams remaining, and they will likely claim one of the two Big 12 title spots heading into a College Football Playoff appearance. The second spot will likely come down to either Texas Tech or BYU.

BYU currently holds a tiebreaker over Texas Tech due to wins over common opponents, according to CBS Sports . If the Red Raiders lose either of their next two games against Baylor or TCU, the Cougars could jump ahead of them. Two wins would earn Texas Tech a trip to the title game. Utah also holds a tiebreaker over BYU in the unlikely case the Utes somehow lose their next two games.

Entering Week 12, no team within the Power Four has clinched a conference championship game appearance. The remaining three Big 12 teams that haven't been eliminated are the Houston Cougars, Arizona Wildcats and Arizona State Sun Devils.

articles.title: Gerard Piqué da la cara por Jesús Owono: "No es el culpable de que todo esto haya pasado"
articles.standfirst: Reflexiona sobre la sanción de 12 partidos impuesta al meta del Andorra y se pregunta: "¿Qué se castiga, la acción o las consecuencias?"
articles.summary: Reflexiona sobre la sanción de 12 partidos impuesta al meta del Andorra y se pregunta: "¿Qué se castiga, la acción o las consecuencias?"
articles.body: Gerard Piqué ha valorado la sanción de 12 partidos impuesta por el Comité de Disciplina Deportiva al guardameta Jesús Owono, por la desafortunada acción que terminó costando la vida al jugador del Tenerife Jesús de Miguel. Una sanción que no va a ser recurrida por expreso deseo de Owono. El presidente del Andorra hace una profunda reflexión sobre la acción que acabó con la muerte de Jesús de Miguel y se hace una pregunta: "¿Qué se castiga, la acción o las consecuencias?". En opinión de Piqué ponerle la sanción máxima a Owono "no es justa". Asegura que la jugada fue un "accidente" y por lo tanto el portero "no es el culpable de lo que acabó pasando". Piqué pone dos ejemplos que también pudieron tener consecuencias trágicas. Una fue la acción vivida en el campo del Albacete el mismo fin de semana de la muerte de Jesús de Miguel, cuando Corpas dio una patada en la cabeza a Quadri, de forma involuntaria, que obligó a llevar al hospital al jugador del Sabadell. Corpas fue expulsado y el Comité sancionó al jugador del Albacete con tres partidos. El otro ejemplo lo vivió en sus propias carnes Gerard Piqué en 2012. En un partido frente al Chelsea, el central quedó inconsciente tras golpearse con Valdés. "Las consecuencias pudieron ser peores de lo que pasó y no por eso fue Valdés el culpable de los sucedido". Este viernes por la tarde recibimos la sanción de 12 partidos por parte del Comité de Competición a Jesús Owono. Vaya por delante que Jesús va a necesitar más de 12 partidos para poder estar disponible y poder competir. No va a haber sanción que nos devuelva a Demi. Ha sido increíble ver la cantidad de muestras de apoyo y cariño por parte de todos sus compañeros, familiares y que el vacío que va a dejar es muy grande. Es evidente que esta situación ha creado un impacto muy grande, ya no en el fútbol español sino a nivel mundial. Es algo totalmente inexplicable que no ha pasado jamás en el fútbol y que aún ahora nos preguntamos por qué. ¿Por qué ha sucedido? Jugadores, exjugadores, entrenadores, porteros... todos lo han calificado de accidente. Creo de verdad que imponer la sanción máxima a Jesús por esta acción lo pone a él en una situación que no se merece porque él no es el culpable de que todo esto haya pasado. Mi reflexión en todo esto es que la sanción de 12 partidos a Jesús Owono me parece que lo que hace es culpabilizar a Jesús de unas consecuencias que él no tuvo la culpa. Creo que la sanción tiene que ser por la acción, no por las consecuencias. Por poneros un ejemplo, ese mismo fin de semana en el campo del Albacete hubo una situación en la que un jugador del Albacete, Corpas, quiso chutar la pelota y le dio una patada en la cabeza a Quadri, un jugador del Sabadell. Por suerte Quadri está bien, las consecuencias en este caso no fueron fatales y el comité de competición ha decidido sancionar con tres partidos a Corpas. Con todo esto mi reflexión va sobre ¿qué se sanciona, la acción o las consecuencias?. Hago este vídeo porque esta situación me ha tocado muy de cerca a nivel personal. Primero estuve en Tenerife cuando sucedió y cuando bajé al vestuario y vi la reacción de nuestros jugadores, entendí que es un impacto que nos va a quedar de por vida a todos los que estábamos ahí. En segundo lugar, porque una situación así yo la he vivido en primera persona. En 2012 en un Barça-Chelsea de semifinales de Champions, yo choqué con mi propio portero, con Víctor Valdés, en una situación muy parecida. Son dos cuerpos que van a mucha velocidad en sentido contrario mirando a la pelota y que de golpe chocan y uno siempre sale más mal parado que el otro. En este caso fui yo, recibí el golpe en la cabeza, intenté seguir jugando sin acordarme de nada, me cambiaron porque me vieron totalmente desorientado y yo no me acuerdo de nada hasta que despierto en el hospital ingresado. Las consecuencias podrían haber sido peores de lo que fue al final. Quedé inconsciente durante un tiempo y tuve que estar en el hospital, pero fue mi propio portero que lo hizo y no por eso Víctor Valdés es el culpable, ni mucho menos y si hubiera pasado algo peor, tampoco lo hubiera sido. Digo todo esto porque la situación que pasó en el campo del Tenerife es muy parecida. Es un portero y un jugador que van mirando la pelota los dos y chocan. Y los humanos muchas veces necesitamos culpar a alguien porque si no, no podemos comprender por qué pasa esto en un terreno de juego. Es un accidente. Creo que imponerle la sanción máxima a Jesús lo pone a él en una situación que no es justa, porque él no es el culpable de lo que acabó pasando.

articles.title: El imparable Bellingham
articles.standfirst: Protagoniza 50 días triunfales con el Madrid y la selección: 13 victorias consecutivas
articles.summary: Protagoniza 50 días triunfales con el Madrid y la selección: 13 victorias consecutivas
articles.body: Bellingham está desatado. Todo lo que toca lo convierte en victoria. Da igual que sea con el Real Madrid o con la selección inglesa. Jude protagoniza 50 días triunfales en los que no ha parado de ganar. Trece victorias consecutivas es su particular trayectoria triunfal desde el pasado 29 de septiembre. Desde entonces, 13 partidos ha jugado y 13 victorias ha conseguido. Ocho con el Real Madrid y cinco con la selección. Es el imparable Bellingham. Además, la racha tiene al inglés como protagonista desde el momento en el que su estrella ha vuelto a brillar. Bellingham está otra vez a un nivel estelar y se ha convertido en pieza clave para Mourinho, en la gran racha que atraviesa el Real Madrid, y para Tuchel, en la espectacular dinámica de la selección inglesa, coronada con el triunfo en el Metropolitano ante España. Jude está subido en la cresta de la ola y no hay quién lo baje. El jugador se siente pletórico y prueba de ello ha sido su participación en esta secuencia triunfal que protagoniza. Ha disputado en los cinco últimos partidos jugados por Inglaterra, siendo titular en cuatro de ellos, y en los ocho últimos del Real Madrid, saliendo de inicio en todos ellos. Un momento ante el que se ha rendido al propio Mourinho. "Bellingham es único. No hay centrocampista en el mundo como él. Es extraordinario. Tiene trabajo, calidad... Excelente". No es para menos, porque el inglés está a un nivel con el que recuerda al de su impactante primera temporada. En esta racha particular de 13 victorias consecutivas, Jude firma tres goles y seis asistencias. En el Madrid, en total, lleva cinco goles, empatado con Güler como el segundo máximo goleador del equipo, sólo superado por el inalcanzable Mbappé. Bellingham vuelve a sentirse exuberante en lo físico y eso le ha catapultado nuevamente a su mejor nivel de juego. "Venía de un año algo difícil, pero aprendí mucho sobre mí mismo. Aprendí cosas que puedo hacer para hacerme la vida más fácil. Siempre me esfuerzo al máximo para ser cada vez mejor", reconocía recientemente. Efectivamente, la pasada temporada las lesiones le frenaron (111 días de baja) y prolongaron un problema (el del hombro) que arrastraba de muchos más atrás, cuando podía jugar pero no hacerlo al ciento por ciento. "Decidí seguir sin operarme y fue un error", admitió. El Mundial fue un punto de inflexión y desde entonces Bellingham no ha levantado el pie del acelerador. En la última cita mundialista marcó siete goles (sólo Mbappé (10) y Messi (8) marcaron más) y lideró a Inglaterra en el tercer puesto obtenido.

articles.title: Xavi da la cara tras el desastre: "No puedo aceptar esto, estoy en shock"
articles.standfirst: El seleccionador de la 'oranje' se mostró muy decepcionado con la actitud de sus jugadores
articles.summary: El seleccionador de la 'oranje' se mostró muy decepcionado con la actitud de sus jugadores
articles.body: Xavi Hernández sufrió su primera derrota como seleccionador de Países Bajos. Pero no fue una derrota cualquiera. Su equipo fue arrollado en Berlín por una Alemania que le quitó el primer puesto de su grupo y que le endosó una manita a la que el técnico español no encuentra explicación: "Ha sido un shock para mí como entrenador. Estoy muy decepcionado, muy triste. No jugamos al fútbol, no tuvimos espíritu. No lo entiendo. No puedo aceptar esto", sentenció. El técnico, que venía de lograr una histórica goleada ante Grecia (7-0), lamentó la falta de actitud de sus jugadores durante distintas fases del partido: "Vamos a construir algo nuevo. La mentalidad debe cambiar. Los valores en el campo deben mejorar. Necesitamos jugadores con garra. Los jugadores deben cambiar su mentalidad. Es una situación difícil, pero los jugadores aprenderán de ella", insistió. Xavi seguía sin salir de su asombro, y más después de lograr ese brillante triunfo ante el combinado heleno hace apenas unos días. "Jugamos un partido histórico contra Grecia el viernes. Un buen partido. Y ahora fue todo lo contrario. Hablé con los jugadores porque intentaba comprender lo que había sucedido". El seleccionador del combinado neerlandés deberá ahora lidiar con las duras críticas que llegan desde los Países Bajos. Declaraciones como las del exjugador Rafael Van der Vaart u otras voces autorizadas que, a buen seguro, aparecerán en las próximas horas. Pero Xavi no fue el único que hizo autocrítica desde dentro del seno de la selección. Denzel Dumfries fue el primero en dar la cara tras el pitido final y reconoció que su equipo no había estado a la altura: "Ha sido una mala actuación nuestra esta noche. Son goles que regalamos con demasiada facilidad, los espacios eran demasiado grandes. Esto no debería ocurrir". Tras la dura derrota sufrida en Berlín, Países Bajos se clasificó para cuartos de final de esta Nations League como segunda de su grupo, por lo que evitará a España. Su posible rival será Francia, Inglaterra o seguramente Portugal, a falta de que los lusos disputen la última jornada de su grupo este martes.

articles.title: Scotland: What's the story with Sebastien Pocognoli, is it now time to go?
articles.summary: The sense of drift in this Scotland team can't go on much longer. Is it too late for Sebastien Pocognoli to win back players and fans?
articles.body:
A few short months ago, Craig Mulholland, the Scottish FA's chief football officer, and Ian Maxwell, the association's chief executive, spoke about the worldwide search for a new Scotland head coach.

The data, the metrics, the cosmic input from the analytics company whose input was received at Hampden as if written on tablets of stone.

The process all pointed to Sebastien Pocognoli being their guy. They paraded him around Hampden, told everybody that loads of clubs were on his tail but that they won the chase.

They may, or may not, have mentioned the word 'coup' but that was certainly what their body language was telling you.

For coup, read boo, the sound surely reverberating around the Tartan Army right now after Monday's 4-0 defeat by Switzerland.

Some nonsense has been written about Pocognoli being on twice the salary that Steve Clarke was on, but whatever they're paying him, there's no value in it so far.

Money is a factor here. Clarke's three qualifications brought a rich bounty into the SFA's coffers, many millions even after deductions. That cash gave the association a little more opportunity to do some of the things they want to do in grassroots football.

A world where Scotland miss out on major championships and the financial windfalls that come with qualification is not a place they want to revisit. The next Euros looks like a gimme - almost harder not to qualify than qualify - but the sense of drift in this team is alarming and can't go on much longer.

Mulholland, Maxwell and let's throw SFA president Mike Mulraney into the mix, should be feeling mightily nervous.

Pocognoli wants patience but Scotland 'don't have time' says Robertson

Pocognoli's abject Scotland suffer 4-0 Nations League defeat in Switzerland

Robertson eclipses Dalglish to become Scotland's most capped man

What do players really think of the coach?

Most people understood that Pocognoli needed time, but implicit in that understanding was a need to see something developing under him, a burgeoning style of play, some positives here and there, a few signs that even though things might not be great today or tomorrow, they're inching in the right direction.

There's been none of that. Decent players look lost. Pocognoli's system has made Scotland a disjointed soft touch. Structural discipline collapses too often. Players charge forward and leave space in behind. He wants hard pressing and maximum intensity, but his players don't look capable of providing it.

In six games they have scored five goals - two from the penalty spot. Promises of jam tomorrow are not cutting it. People can see a team on the slide.

In Switzerland, there was a drubbing that piles the heat on the Belgian, on the people who appointed him and on the players, too.

If the chaos on the field wasn't a bad enough look for Pocognoli, then some of the words said in the wake of this objectionable 4-0 pummelling to a Switzerland B side playing in third gear only made things worse.

Andy Robertson, on the night he became Scotland's most capped player in history, delivered a damning riff that sounded strongly like a commentary on this coaching regime and this set of players.

In his stead, John McGinn did much the same thing. "You don't get time" was the gist. Who doesn't get time?

Robertson and McGinn didn't lay it on the line, but their thoughts resembled distress flares. These Scotland players can be overhyped, but they are better than some of the nonsense they dished up in St Gallen.

More than one former Scotland international reckoned they saw players not exactly busting a gut out there. These guys know the tell-tale signs.

Some private conversations between the SFA hierarchy and the senior operators in this team need to take place. What were they suggesting in the post-match? What are they really thinking?

An honesty session behind closed doors needs to take place long before the qualification campaign for the next Euros begins in March.

Pocognoli comes across as a good person: open, communicative, passionate and hard-working.

He also appears stubborn in the way he sets up his team, a system that is so easily exploited by more experienced coaches, people like Switzerland boss Murat Yakin, who was missing a battalion of heavy hitters and yet still won this game at a canter.

Yakin started six players who had six caps or fewer to their name - three of them scored.

McGinn said later that Scotland were in this movie before in the early days of Clarke's tenure, mentioning the 4-0 loss to Russia in 2019 - four goals conceded in 27 minutes.

The difference between Clarke and Pocognoli is obvious. Clarke had vast experience and the nous to fix the problems. Pocognoli is a young coach with no such back story, no such track record in turning bad situations into good.

Pocognoli said later that people should look beyond the result, to the "attitude of the players" who were at times "brilliant, brave and on the front foot".

He argued that 4-0 wasn't a true reflection of the game, referring to the glaring misses by Lewis Ferguson and Scott McTominay. Scotland were 3-0 down at the time. He didn't think the loss had anything to do with a system or a lack of confidence or a lack of belief.

Not many fans were buying what he was selling. Listening to some of his players, you doubted that they were buying it either.

After the home loss to Slovenia, Robertson said his team had been "out-played" and "out-fought." There were some other comments made after the desperately stodgy 2-1 win over North Macedonia on Friday. On Monday, it cranked up another level.

McGinn was asked if he felt Scotland were on the right path. "Impossible for me to say yes," he replied. It was hard to listen to what the players were trying to say and conclude that everybody's on the same page in this set-up.

Intransigence is not a good characteristic for any manager. In recent times we've seen a few bosses at big clubs who were wedded to their principles. Russell Martin and Wilfried Nancy didn't last long at Rangers and Celtic.

To repeat Robertson's line, you don't get time.

Clarke had an instinctive understanding of that and pragmatism was his way of taking his team forward, difficult yard by difficult yard. Rigid idealism is not a sensible way to operate, but Pocognoli has gone down that road in his first six games.

It's a dead-end down there. He needs to turn back and find another way while he still can. If he still can.

articles.title: Illes Balears Palma jugará mañana la semifinal ante el Carlos Barbosa
articles.standfirst: Evita al Sporting Clube, tras golear al Pato Futsal (1-5), que se medirá ante los anfitriones
articles.summary: Evita al Sporting Clube, tras golear al Pato Futsal (1-5), que se medirá ante los anfitriones
articles.body: El Illes Balears Palma Futsal jugará mañana miércoles (21:00) la primera semifinal de la Copa Intercontinental ante A Carlos Barbosa Futsal tras imponerse en el segundo partido de la primera fase al anfitrión, Pato Futsal (1-5). De esta forma, los palmesanos evitan al Sporting Clube de Portugal, que se medirá a los anfitriones en la segunda. Este triunfo es el décimo que encarrilan los de Antonio Vadillo (dos en esta Intercontinental que se suman a los ocho en Liga) en un partido en el que el de ayer ante el Al-Ula se mostraron muy superiores en cuanto se demostraron los roles que cada equipo iba a desempeñar en el partido. Al Pato Futsal le pesó el hecho de tener 5.000 aficionados tratando de llevarles en volandas y, con sus incorporaciones de Djony como quinto jugador en ataque trataron de sorprender a la firme defensa palmesana. Curiosamente, sería el propio Djony quien se tendría que desdoblar parando los ataques de los de Vadillo hasta que Carlos Gómez, tras recibir de Dennis Cavalcanti finalizaba soberbiamente la jugada. Confirmando que Illes Balears se siente muy cómodo en este tipo de partidos en tierras brasileñas, no olvidemos que la primera Intercontinental ante Cascavél, siguió ampliando su ventaja gracias a Diego Nunes en un balón parado servido por Júlio Zanotto y Deivao. De hecho la primera intervención clara de Dennis Cavalcanti fue cuando el primer tiempo expiraba. Por si necesitaba más tranquilidad, Deivao hizo el 0-4. En el segundo tiempo, que se endureció algo más que el primero, el único problema fueron las faltas, ya que cometió cinco mediado este periodo y tuvo que bajar un punto la intensidad para evitar los lanzamientos de 10 metros. Pato Futsal acabó el partido con Dudu como portero jugador y, combinando la defensa 2-2 y 1-2-1 ante el ataque brasileño. Pato encontró un pase a Biel, todavía con 95 segundos por jugarse que fue el 1-4. La última pérdida de balón fue castigada por Deivao, que culminó su 'hat-trick' con el 1-5 FICHA TÉCNICA Arena Cláudio Petrycovski 5.000 espectadores PATO FUTSAL: Djony; Dudu, Duduzinho, Biel y Pedro Carioca. También jugaron: Max, Jhonnas, Léo Catolé, Vitinho, Micael y Renato (p. s.) ENTRENADOR: Luciano Bonfim. ILLES BALEARS PALMA: Dennis Cavalcanti; Piqueras, Ernesto, Diego Nunes y Fabinho. También jugaron: Machado, Deivao, Piqueras, Lucao, Alisson Neves, Charuto, David Peña, Carlos Gómez y Júlio Zanotto. ENTRENADOR: Antonio Vadillo. GOLES.0-1 9' Carlos Gómez. 0-2 15' Diego Nunes. 0-3 19' Deivao. 0-4 32' Deivao 1-4 39' Biel. 1-5 40' Deivao.
