articles.title: Former USMNT coach says 'American sports reward losers' as he leaves for Manchester United
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino says American sports reward losers, blasting Major League Soccer's lack of promotion and relegation as he departs the USMNT.
articles.body: Americans are used to dominating just about every sport we care about, which makes our ongoing mediocrity in men’s soccer tough to swallow. As former USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino heads to Manchester United after 26 months in charge, his takeaways from running U.S. soccer are a bad look for the program. Coming from European football, trying to build a winner inside a system that cushions failure was a problem from day one. He summed up America's dilemma with soccer to Spanish newspaper El País during the 2026 World Cup. "American sports reward losers," he said. THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW! Over in Europe, losing gets your club relegated and puts jobs on the line. In Major League Soccer, nobody gets booted out of the league, and finishing in the cellar just gets you rewarded with a top draft pick. That setup completely kills the survival instinct you need to win at the highest level. MAURICIO POCHETTINO TOLD USMNT PLAYERS 'WE'RE AMERICAN, WE DON'T TAKE S***' AHEAD OF WORLD CUP "If you start in MLS and you haven’t won a game in three months and you’re at the bottom, what’s the consequence if there’s no promotion or relegation, no international competition? Pochettino said. "Soccer is different: if you reward those who don’t win, if you don’t have goals, you don’t fight. If I lose, what happens? Nothing. They just fire the coach." Hard to argue with the guy. American sports fans have been calling this out for years: U.S. soccer is overly corporate and flat-out soft when real trophies are on the line. LA GALAXY COACH GREG VANNEY SAYS TEAM USA WAS 'TOO NAIVE,' EXPLAINS CHRISTIAN PULISIC'S STRUGGLES "Also, the American player is disciplined, but with a sense of complacency that isn’t good in soccer," he said. "It took us a year and a half to change that mentality." Nowhere was that battle against complacency more obvious than how Pochettino handled Christian Pulisic. LANDON DONOVAN JOINS CHRISTIAN PULISIC CRITICISM FOLLOWING USA'S WORLD CUP EXIT WITH HARSH OBSERVATION After Pulisic decided to sit out the 2025 CONCACAF Gold Cup, where the U.S. watched Mexico win the title in the final, Pochettino refused to give his most talented player the captain’s armband. He rolled with veteran Tim Ream at the 2026 World Cup, then passed over Pulisic again in October in favor of Tyler Adams. Pulisic can take over a game when he’s locked in, but putting up zero goals at a World Cup after taking a voluntary summer off raises fair questions about whether America’s biggest star has the grit to actually lead. Even while keeping things friendly with the American soccer press corps, he clearly got tired of coverage that graded the team on a soft curve instead of holding players to real international standards. "I understand the culture of football," Pochettino insisted. To be fair, Pochettino’s point only goes so far. America’s closed-league setup keeps franchises financially stable instead of letting clubs go bankrupt like they do in Europe, and the USMNT’s 4-1 Round of 16 loss to Belgium showed that a tougher attitude won’t close a talent gap overnight. TEAM USA ISSUES STATEMENT IN ENGLISH AND SPANISH AFTER DISASTROUS WORLD CUP EXIT As U.S. Soccer starts looking at potential successors like Steve Cherundolo, B.J. Callaghan, Pellegrino Matarazzo and former Manchester City boss Pep Guardiola, whom Pochettino recommended for the job. Until U.S. soccer stops protecting players from failure, this program is going to stay an afterthought when the real heavyweights show up. articles.body:
Butch Jones endured one firing from Tennessee nearly a decade ago . Now Arkansas State football has canned him following a 4-6 start. With the Saturday Coastal Carolina contest now representing his final game with the Red Wolves.

Jones lasts six seasons with the Sun Belt Conference school. But he never achieved the success he delivered at his previous stops including in Knoxville. Jones' Red Wolves teams went 30-43 overall. He took two Arkansas State teams to a bowl game, including the 2025 XBox Bowl.

Jones has compiled a 114-97 overall record that includes stops with Central Michigan, Cincinnati and Tennessee. He even won Big East Coach of the Year honors in 2011 before those teams helped form the American Athletic Conference.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Arkansas State creates the seventh different Football Bowl Subdivision opening in 2026. Although North Carolina State immediately filled its vacancy with school legend and former NFL Pro Bowl quarterback Philip Rivers. Meanwhile, Maryland interviewed former LSU, Notre Dame, Cincinnati and Central Michigan coach Brian Kelly for its vacancy.

But now the focus in Jonesboro shifts to who succeeds Jones. Arkansas State could be monitoring what's happening with Southern Miss and former coach Blake Anderson, who owns a worse 3-7 record. Anderson, though, is the Red Wolves' most successful coach who guided six straight bowl appearances from 2014 to 2019. Perhaps Anderson becomes a one-and-done with the Golden Eagles.

Elsewhere, Dave Doeren is available after his dismissal from NC State where he became that school's all-time wins leader. Doeren coached at a Group of Five school before in Northern Illinois and owns 121-77 mark.

Arkansas State may even attract school legend Ryan Alpin, currently the offensive coordinator at Georgia Southern. His offense is 40th overall but averaging 32.7 points per game. He broke records from 2009 to 2012 in Jonesboro.
